permutationLabel: Immunosuppressed (renal transplant: tacrolimus, MMF, prednisolone) — masked signs, gangrenous change = Grade II
summary: 58-year-old renal transplant recipient on tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisolone 7.5 mg: 2 days of mild RUQ discomfort, T 37.6 °C, minimal tenderness, WBC 11.2, CRP 145; ultrasound shows gallstones with a striated, irregular wall and intraluminal membranes (gangrenous change).

inputs.chiefComplaint: Right upper abdominal discomfort for two days
inputs.hpi: Renal transplant 6 years ago, stable graft. Two days of mild right upper quadrant discomfort and malaise, low-grade temperature, nausea. Takes tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisolone 7.5 mg daily. Known gallstones on a surveillance scan last year.

exam.general: Cushingoid. Temperature 37.6°C, pulse 96/min, BP 128/76. Transplant kidney in the right iliac fossa non-tender.
exam.abdomen: Mild right upper quadrant tenderness; Murphy's sign weakly positive. No guarding.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Gallstones. Gallbladder wall striated and irregular (8 mm) with intraluminal membranes and pericholecystic fluid — features of gangrenous cholecystitis. No intramural gas. CBD 5 mm.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute calculous cholecystitis (gangrenous)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute gangrenous calculous cholecystitis, Tokyo (TG18) Grade II (marked local inflammation) in an immunosuppressed renal transplant recipient; signs masked by steroids.

emergencyLevel.note: Gangrenous change in an immunosuppressed patient: perforation risk; same-day surgical decision. iOS (predicted, not observed): routine.

redFlags.note: Immunosuppression masks fever, pain and leucocytosis.
redFlags.knownGapNote: No output mentions immunosuppression, transplant or steroids.
redFlags.proposedFix: clinical-inference.ts: add an immunosuppression prompt (tacrolimus/mycophenolate/azathioprine/prednisolone ≥5 mg or "transplant" in PMH/medications): masked signs, lower threshold for imaging/escalation, steroid cover, drug interactions.

values.note: Marked local inflammation (gangrenous cholecystitis) is on its own a Grade II criterion.
values.knownGapNote: Web calculator returns Grade I: no "marked local inflammation" (gangrenous) criterion.
values.proposedFix: clinical-scores.ts scoreTokyoCholecystitis: add the missing TG18 Grade II criteria (duration >72 h, palpable tender RUQ mass, marked local inflammation — gangrenous/emphysematous/abscess/biliary peritonitis) as inputs, as ScalesTab/ClinicalScoresPanel ticks.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: No peri-operative steroid cover for a patient on prednisolone 7.5 mg.
mustInclude.proposedFix: See flag-immunosuppression; add peri-operative hydrocortisone cover (AAGBI/RCP/SfE 2020) to operative-plan templates when a glucocorticoid is on the medication list.

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Appendicectomy operative plan fires on "No guarding" in the exam text.
mustExclude.proposedFix: clinical-inference.ts SURGICAL PATHWAY CASCADE: gate hasAppendicitisIndication/hasGallstoneIndication on the working diagnosis or assessment (as the Alvarado block already does with assessmentHasAppend) and on positive, non-negated findings — not on any "guarding", "gallbladder wall" or "gallstone" substring.

dxVariant.knownGapNote: Grade I variant selected ("cholecystitis" keyword first; "gangrenous cholecystitis" is a Grade III keyword in dx-variants although TG18 grades it II).
dxVariant.proposedFix: dx-variants.ts: check Grade III → II → I and move "gangrenous cholecystitis" to Grade II (TG18 marked local inflammation), keeping Grade III for organ dysfunction.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — diagnostic criteria and severity grading of acute cholecystitis
guideline.section: Diagnostic criteria (A local + B systemic + C imaging); Grade II: WBC >18,000/mm³, palpable tender RUQ mass, duration >72 h, marked local inflammation (gangrenous, emphysematous, abscess, biliary peritonitis); Grade III: organ dysfunction
guideline.citation: Yokoe M, Hata J, Takada T, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:41–54.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — flowchart for the management of acute cholecystitis
guideline.section: Grade I: early LC if CCI ≤5 / ASA-PS ≤2; Grade II: early LC in an advanced centre if fit, otherwise antibiotics and urgent/early gallbladder drainage when not responding; Grade III: organ support, antibiotics, drainage unless favourable organ dysfunction
guideline.citation: Okamoto K, Suzuki K, Takada T, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:55–72.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — antimicrobial therapy for acute cholangitis and cholecystitis
guideline.section: Blood cultures in Grade II/III; antimicrobial choice by severity; duration after source control
guideline.citation: Gomi H, Solomkin JS, Schlossberg D, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:3–16.

guideline.name: AAGBI/RCP/Society for Endocrinology guideline — peri-operative glucocorticoids in adrenal insufficiency (including long-term steroid users)
guideline.section: Patients on ≥5 mg prednisolone for >4 weeks need peri-operative hydrocortisone cover
guideline.citation: Woodcock T, Barker P, Daniel S, et al. Anaesthesia. 2020;75:654–663.

rationale: Permutation: immunosuppression. Mild symptoms and a near-normal WBC hide gangrenous cholecystitis, which TG18 grades II on imaging alone. Tests urgency without florid signs, the marked-local-inflammation criterion, and peri-operative steroid/transplant considerations.
